articles.headline: RBI approves record Rs 2.11 lakh crore dividend to central government
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India approved a surplus transfer of Rs 2,10,874 crore to the government for FY24, more than double the previous year's transfer. This unexpected windfall is significantly higher than the government's budget estimate of Rs 1.02 lakh crore, providing a major fiscal cushion to help achieve the 5.1% fiscal deficit target and potentially increase infrastructure spending.

articles.headline: Sensex gains 268 points as record RBI dividend boosts investor sentiment
articles.summary: Indian equity benchmarks Sensex and Nifty closed higher on Wednesday, fueled by the RBI's record dividend announcement. The Sensex rose 268.47 points to settle at 74,221.06, while the Nifty 50 ended at 22,597.80. Banking and financial stocks led the rally, as the massive surplus transfer improved market outlook on the government's fiscal health and borrowing requirements.

articles.headline: Pune police seek adult trial for juvenile in fatal Porsche crash
articles.summary: Authorities in Pune have moved the sessions court to try a 17-year-old involved in a fatal Porsche crash as an adult. The minor allegedly killed two techies while driving under the influence. The case has sparked national outrage over the lenient bail conditions initially granted by the Juvenile Justice Board, leading to the arrest of the teen's father and a crackdown on local pubs.

articles.headline: Severe heatwave continues as Delhi temperatures soar to 47.8 degrees Celsius
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert for North India as a severe heatwave intensified across Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi. Mungeshpur in Delhi recorded a peak of 47.8 degrees. Power demand in the national capital hit an all-time high of 7,717 MW. The government has advised citizens to avoid sun exposure as the heatwave is expected to persist for several more days.

articles.headline: Campaigning peaks for Phase 6 of Lok Sabha elections across 58 seats
articles.summary: Political activity intensified as campaigning reached its final stages for the sixth phase of polling on May 25. This phase covers 58 constituencies across 8 states and UTs, including all 7 seats in Delhi. Key candidates include Manoj Tiwari, Kanhaiya Kumar, and Mehbooba Mufti. Prime Minister Modi and INDIA bloc leaders exchanged barbs over the constitution, reservation, and unemployment.

articles.headline: InterGlobe Aviation shares surge amid reports of promoter stake sale plan
articles.summary: Shares of InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo) jumped over 3% following reports that co-founder Rakesh Gangwal is likely to sell a portion of his stake via block deals. Despite engine supply issues, the carrier remains dominant with over 60% market share. Analysts remain bullish on the airline due to strong yield management and international expansion plans despite the potential promoter exit.

articles.headline: Sun Pharma reports 34% rise in Q4 profit to Rs 2,654 crore
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries reported a 34% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit for the fourth quarter. Total revenue grew 9% to Rs 11,813 crore, driven by strong growth in the specialty business in the US and the chronic segment in India. The company recommended a final dividend of Rs 5 per share. Growth in emerging markets and global generic sales remained stable.

articles.headline: NHAI identifies highway stretches worth Rs 54,000 crore for monetization
articles.summary: The National Highways Authority of India has identified 33 highway stretches spanning 2,741 km for monetization in the current fiscal year. The authority aims to raise Rs 54,000 crore through Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) models and InvITs. The move is intended to unlock capital for new greenfield expressways and reduce the authority's debt burden while maintaining infrastructure quality.

articles.headline: Google to begin Pixel 8 smartphone manufacturing in India
articles.summary: Google has announced plans to start manufacturing its flagship Pixel 8 smartphones in India, partnering with international and domestic manufacturers. This move aligns with the 'Make in India' initiative and mirrors strategies by Apple and Samsung to diversify supply chains. The production is expected to begin in 2024, helping Google serve the growing demand for premium devices in India.

articles.headline: Rural demand recovery helps FMCG companies achieve volume growth in Q4
articles.summary: FMCG companies noted a significant recovery in rural markets during the January-March quarter, with volume growth in rural areas outpacing urban markets for the first time in two years. Lower inflation and a recovery in farm incomes helped boost demand for staples and smaller packs. Companies like HUL and Dabur remain optimistic about further recovery given the forecast of a normal monsoon.

articles.headline: Dollar deluge prompts RBI to end FCNR scheme early
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India decided to end its foreign currency borrowing window for non-resident Indians ahead of schedule after deposits hit $52.3 billion in just 67 days. The scheme was initially launched to stabilize the rupee by attracting dollar inflows, but the massive response created excess liquidity, prompting the central bank to halt the window a month early.

articles.headline: China’s high-tech boom seen failing to halt slowdown
articles.summary: Official data indicates that China's economy struggled in the first half of 2026 as a high-tech manufacturing surge failed to offset a deep property slump and weak domestic consumption. Industrial production growth slowed while fixed-asset investment missed expectations, raising concerns that the nation's high-tech pivot isn't enough to sustain overall growth targets.

articles.headline: Centre takes the scalpel to cosmetic care's Wild West
articles.summary: The Indian government has issued strict new guidelines for the $2.1 billion cosmetic surgery and skin treatment market. The rules mandate that procedures like Botox, fillers, and laser treatments must only be performed by qualified medical specialists in registered clinics. The move aims to curb risks from untrained practitioners in the rapidly growing aesthetic care sector.

articles.headline: Equities slide during week as Tata jitters, metal rout
articles.summary: Indian stock markets faced a volatile week as investor sentiment was dampened by uncertainty surrounding the Tata Group's leadership transition and a global rout in metal prices. The Sensex and Nifty recorded weekly losses despite a tentative return of foreign portfolio investors, as high-valuation concerns and sector-specific pressures weighed on the broader market.

articles.headline: India opens nuclear sector to proven foreign tech
articles.summary: In a major policy shift, India has proposed allowing private sector participation in the nuclear power industry and opening the doors to proven foreign reactor technologies. The move is designed to accelerate the country's transition to clean energy and meet ambitious net-zero targets by leveraging international expertise and private capital in the regulated sector.

articles.headline: Fertilizer subsidy bill rises as crops absorb barely 40%
articles.summary: India's fertilizer subsidy costs are rising even as research reveals that crops absorb only 30% to 40% of the nitrogen applied. The inefficient usage is leading to significant groundwater contamination and air pollution. Experts are calling for a shift toward balanced nutrient use and better technology to reduce the fiscal burden and environmental impact of subsidized urea.

articles.headline: BSNL Q1 loss widens as expenses outpace revenue
articles.summary: State-run Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd (BSNL) reported a consolidated net loss of ₹1,280 crore for the June quarter, widening from ₹1,007 crore in the previous year. While the company saw a modest rise in revenue from operations, it was offset by a 5.5% increase in total expenses, particularly in employee costs and network maintenance as it continues its 4G and 5G rollout.

articles.headline: Jindal Steel targets 21 mt capacity by 2032
articles.summary: Jindal Steel and Power has set an ambitious target to reach 21 million tonnes of annual steelmaking capacity by 2032. New managing director V.R. Sharma emphasized a focus on operational stability, raw material security, and the production of green steel to meet evolving global environmental standards while expanding the company's domestic footprint.

articles.headline: Ten Freedoms Gen Z wants for India's future
articles.summary: On India's 80th Independence Day, young Indians reflect on the evolving meaning of freedom. The feature highlights Gen Z's desire for the freedom to live without labels, experiment with careers, and challenge institutional systems. The stories reflect a generational shift toward valuing individual identity, mental health, and social accountability over traditional societal norms.

articles.headline: The menopause blind spot in public health policy
articles.summary: Health experts are urging the Indian government to include menopause care in public health programs as the number of women in the 45-49 age group is set to reach 47 million by 2030. Currently, menopause is often ignored in health policy, leading to a lack of support for symptoms that affect the physical and psychological well-being of millions of women.

articles.headline: When Gen A starts chasing perfect skin
articles.summary: Dermatologists are raising alarms over 'cosmeticorexia' among pre-teens and children who are increasingly using intensive anti-aging skincare products. Driven by social media trends, many children are applying active ingredients like retinol and AHAs that can damage young skin. Experts call for better parental supervision and age-appropriate skincare routines.

articles.headline: Milk-based drinks get a fresh pour for consumers
articles.summary: Leading FMCG firms including Hindustan Unilever and Varun Beverages are expanding their ready-to-drink milk beverage portfolios. As consumers move away from sugary carbonated drinks, there is a growing demand for protein-rich, fortified milk options. The market for dairy-based beverages in India is estimated to be growing at 18% annually.

articles.headline: Gangster wanted for '24 Delhi drug haul brought back from UAE
articles.summary: The Narcotics Control Bureau brought back fugitive Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE. He is accused of coordinating an international narcotics trafficking network involving over 1,800kg of mephedrone. Basoya was taken into custody at IGI Airport on Friday after fleeing the country following his name emerging in multiple major drug cases earlier this year.

articles.headline: India at 79: Challenges of demographics and employment prospects
articles.summary: Data analysis reveals that while India has the largest young population globally, its median age is increasing. The economy faces a key task in generating well-paying salaried jobs, as nearly half of private salaried workers lack written contracts or social security. Employment is shifting from farming to non-agricultural sectors, requiring urgent policy focus on job quality.

articles.headline: President underlines push to protect exams and secure youth future
articles.summary: Addressing the nation on the eve of the 80th Independence Day, President Droupadi Murmu highlighted government efforts to end unfair practices in public examinations. She emphasized that exams are gateways to opportunities for the youth and outlined the country's progress toward 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047, noting the role of digital transformation and economic reforms.

articles.headline: Luigi Mangione admits in court to killing health insurance exec
articles.summary: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty in a US federal court to the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in Manhattan. Mangione admitted to targeting Thompson with the intent to kill. The guilty plea will allow him to avoid a federal trial, though he still faces state murder charges. His actions had triggered a national debate over the U.S. health insurance system.

articles.headline: Delhi 2047 master plan pitches for traffic congestion charges
articles.summary: The Delhi Development Authority's Master Plan 2047 proposes introducing congestion pricing for private vehicles in identified high-traffic areas. The plan also includes pricing for on-street parking to regulate private vehicle use and promote transit-oriented development. The document aims to guide the city's growth and infrastructure through the mid-21st century.

articles.headline: Union Health Minister Nadda admitted to AIIMS Delhi; condition stable
articles.summary: Union Health Minister JP Nadda was admitted to AIIMS Delhi for a heart procedure after experiencing chest discomfort. Hospital sources confirmed his condition is stable following a coronary angiography. He is currently under observation in the cardiology department. Nadda, 63, had previously been admitted for similar tests in February 2024.

articles.headline: Two commercial ships with Indian crew members attacked in Hormuz
articles.summary: Two commercial vessels, the MT Navig8 Meteor and MT Tanit, were attacked with projectiles while passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Both ships had Indian crew members on board, including a total of 130 Indians across several vessels in the region. No injuries were reported, and the vessels are safe. The UAE has denounced the incidents as 'hostile attacks'.

articles.headline: India issues draft rules for private sector nuclear power projects
articles.summary: The Indian government has issued a draft regulatory framework to allow private sector participation in nuclear power projects. The rules aim to attract investment and foreign technology while maintaining strict regulatory oversight. This move is seen as a key step toward diversifying India's energy mix and achieving its clean energy targets by 2047.

articles.headline: World must focus on Pakistan-backed terrorism in J&K: India
articles.summary: India's external affairs ministry stated that the international community must focus on Pakistan's continued support for terrorism in Jammu & Kashmir and PoK. The statement came following a visit by the Norwegian foreign minister to Islamabad. India reiterated its stand that terrorism and talks cannot go together and urged countries to respect its territorial integrity.

articles.headline: MEA urges respect for Italy ties amid political row over remarks
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs called for mutual respect in diplomatic ties with Italy following a political controversy. The row erupted over derogatory remarks made by some Indian politicians regarding the Italian Prime Minister. The MEA emphasized that the relationship between the two nations is strong and should not be undermined by individual social media comments.

articles.headline: Karnataka MLA's daughter booked for slapping woman police officer
articles.summary: A case was registered against the daughter of a Karnataka MLA for allegedly slapping a woman sub-inspector in Mandya. The incident occurred during crowd control at a temple when the MLA's daughter reportedly lost her temper after being stopped by the officer. The MLA later issued a public apology for his daughter's conduct, and the police are investigating the matter.

articles.headline: BJP opposes proposed Bengaluru parking charges for outside houses
articles.summary: The BJP in Karnataka protested against the government's proposal to charge residents for parking their vehicles on roads outside their homes. The proposed 'parking permit' fees could range from Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 per year. BJP leaders termed it a 'looting policy' and demanded its immediate withdrawal, citing the burden on middle-class residents.

articles.headline: Four arrested for killing Dalit man in Bidar after crop dispute
articles.summary: Police in Bidar arrested four men for the murder of a 42-year-old Dalit man following a dispute over agricultural crops. The accused allegedly assaulted the victim with a sickle and heavy sticks, leading to his death. Cases have been registered under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and murder charges. The state government has promised strict action against the culprits.

articles.headline: BJP protests lack of women ministers in expanded Karnataka cabinet
articles.summary: BJP legislators in Karnataka staged a protest against the Congress government for failing to include women in the recently expanded state cabinet. Protesters raised slogans demanding 33% reservation for women in the legislative body and cabinet. The BJP accused the government of neglecting women's representation despite its poll promises regarding women's empowerment.

articles.headline: High Court seeks Lokayukta response in Kharge trust land case
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court sought a response from the Lokayukta regarding a petition alleging irregularities in land allotment to a trust linked to Mallikarjun Kharge. The petition claims that the Bangalore Development Authority allotted 2 acres of land to the trust at a 50% concession, despite it not having prior experience in education or research as required by rules.

articles.headline: KPSC to adopt tech-driven system to speed up job recruitment
articles.summary: The Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) announced it will adopt a technology-driven system to streamline and accelerate the job recruitment process. The new system includes online OMR sheet scanning and automated result generation to reduce delays. The KPSC aims to complete the selection process for various government posts within five months of notification.

articles.headline: AIADMK stages protest against Karnataka's Cauvery reservoir project
articles.summary: AIADMK leaders in Tamil Nadu staged a protest against Karnataka's plan to build a reservoir at Mekedatu across the Cauvery river. The party claimed the project would severely affect the flow of water to Tamil Nadu farmers. Protesters urged the central government to intervene and stop Karnataka from proceeding with any construction on the river without the consent of lower riparian states.

articles.headline: Andhra High Court declares arrests of two in liquor scam illegal
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh High Court declared the arrests of two key accused in an alleged liquor scam case as illegal. The court found that the Special Investigation Team (SIT) had not followed the mandatory procedures for arrest and failed to provide sufficient grounds. The accused were allegedly involved in irregularities in the procurement and sale of liquor during the previous government's tenure.

articles.headline: Supreme Court upholds clean chit to CM Naidu in land case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court upheld a high court order quashing a criminal case against Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu regarding an alleged land pooling fraud in Amaravati. The court noted that the allegations were politically motivated and did not establish any legal malice. The bench emphasized that the judiciary should not be used as a platform for political battles.

articles.headline: Chennai city body revokes increase in property tax rates
articles.summary: The Greater Chennai Corporation announced it would revoke the recently implemented increase in property tax rates following widespread public opposition. The city body clarified that it would only carry out a 'reassessment' of properties rather than a general rate hike. The move is expected to provide relief to residents who had complained about the sudden financial burden.

articles.headline: Telangana approves rs 200-cr scheme for electric auto conversions
articles.summary: The Telangana government approved a Rs 200 crore scheme to provide subsidies for converting nearly 18,700 petrol and diesel-powered autos into electric ones. The initiative aims to reduce vehicular pollution in the Hyderabad core region. Each eligible auto driver will be provided a subsidy of up to Rs 1.50 lakh to facilitate the transition to green energy.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh rejects revised Krishna water-sharing pacts
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh told the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal it would not accept any revised water-sharing agreements that reduce its allocated share of 512 TMC. The state argued that the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, fixed the water shares and any change would be a violation of the law. Telangana has been seeking a revision of the water shares based on the current river basin parameters.

articles.headline: Human-elephant conflicts log fatality spike in South India
articles.summary: A report by the Wildlife Institute of India reveals that human-elephant conflicts caused 130 deaths in South India during 2023-24. Tamil Nadu recorded the highest number of deaths (59), followed by Karnataka (48). The report highlights that infrastructure projects, habitat fragmentation, and the expansion of agriculture into forest fringes are key drivers of the increasing conflict.

articles.headline: PM Modi marks Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi marked Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, stating that the event tore apart millions of lives and families. He paid tribute to those who suffered and emphasized the need to remember the historical tragedy to prevent its recurrence. Several events were held across the country to honor the memory of those who lost their lives during the partition in 1947.

articles.headline: Privilege notices filed against Rahul Gandhi in Lok Sabha
articles.summary: Two separate privilege notices were filed against Rahul Gandhi for his remarks in the Lok Sabha targeting the Union Home Minister regarding the anti-paper leak bill. The BJP legislators who filed the notices accused Gandhi of making 'baseless and leveling' allegations. The Lok Sabha Speaker has sought a response from Gandhi on the matter within a specified timeframe.

articles.headline: Devendra Fadnavis uses heritage temple visits to connect with Gen-Z
articles.summary: Maharashtra Deputy CM Devendra Fadnavis has launched an initiative to visit 1,000 heritage temples in the state to connect with younger generations. The program involves sharing social media content and videos explaining the historical and architectural significance of these sites. The move is seen as an effort to promote cultural heritage while engaging with the youth ahead of assembly polls.

articles.headline: SAD chief Sukhbir Badal alleges forces want to disturb Punjab peace
articles.summary: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal stated he is not afraid of threats and alleged that 'certain forces' are attempting to create unrest in Punjab. His comments came after a reported attack at a gurdwara in Amritsar. Badal called on the state government to maintain communal harmony and ensure that elements trying to disrupt the peace are dealt with strictly.

articles.headline: Defense ministry signs contracts worth rs 1,577-cr for kamikaze drones
articles.summary: The defense ministry signed contracts worth Rs 1,577 crore to procure kamikaze drones for the Indian Army. The drones, also known as loitering munitions, are expected to enhance the army's precision strike capabilities. The procurement is part of a larger plan to modernize the military with indigenous unmanned aerial systems for surveillance and combat roles.

articles.headline: Parliamentary panel flags vacancies in leadership of govt-run firms
articles.summary: A parliamentary panel expressed serious concern over the significant number of vacancies in leadership roles at central public sector enterprises (CPSEs). The report highlighted that 70% of 158 CPSEs are operating without full-time chairpersons or directors. The panel called for urgent steps to fill these roles to ensure the efficient functioning and strategic direction of these firms.

articles.headline: UGC-NET 2026 provisional answer key to be released soon
articles.summary: The National Testing Agency (NTA) announced that the provisional answer keys for the UGC-NET 2026 exam will be released shortly on its official website. Candidates will be given an opportunity to challenge the keys before the final results are declared. The exam was conducted in multiple phases across the country for assistant professorships and junior research fellowships.

articles.headline: Adani and BEML partner to manufacture LCH fuselages for HAL
articles.summary: Adani Defense and BEML Limited have entered into a partnership to manufacture fuselages for the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) for Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL). The collaboration aims to increase the production capacity for the LCH, which is being inducted into the Indian Army and Air Force. The fuselages will be produced at a new facility in Bengaluru, supporting the 'Make in India' initiative.

articles.headline: UGC introduces substance abuse awareness course for university students
articles.summary: The University Grants Commission (UGC) is introducing a mandatory 30-hour course on substance abuse awareness for all undergraduate and postgraduate students. The curriculum aims to educate students on the neurobiological and psychosocial impacts of addiction. The course will be part of the 'Viksit Bharat' initiative to promote a healthy and drug-free environment in educational institutions.

articles.headline: Supreme Court imposes rs 10L cost on Reliance Industries
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a plea by Reliance Industries to redact certain parts of a witness affidavit in its 2004 dispute with NTPC over gas supply. The court imposed a Rs 10 lakh fine on the company, stating that the petition was an attempt to delay proceedings. The fine amount will be deposited with the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association to support legal aid services.

articles.headline: Three tourists killed in Nainital road accident as vehicle falls into gorge
articles.summary: Three tourists, including a 10-month-old infant, were killed and 19 others injured when their vehicle fell into a deep gorge in Nainital, Uttarakhand. The group was traveling from Faridabad when the accident occurred on a winding stretch of road. Local residents and emergency teams conducted rescue operations, and the injured were admitted to nearby hospitals for treatment.

articles.headline: Two college girls drown while filming reel in Maharashtra dam
articles.summary: Two college girls drowned in the Borgaon dam in Maharashtra's Yavatmal district while allegedly filming a social media reel. One of the girls fell into the water while taking a selfie, and her friend jumped in to save her; both were swept away by strong currents. Local divers recovered the bodies several hours later. Police have urged people to exercise caution near water bodies during the monsoon.

articles.headline: Four die after inhaling toxic gas inside well in Bihar
articles.summary: Four people, including a man and his son, died in Bihar's Gaya district after inhaling toxic gas while trying to repair a water pump inside an old well. The victims reportedly lost consciousness due to the high concentration of methane and other gases. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary expressed grief over the incident and announced an ex-gratia of Rs 4 lakh each for the kin of the deceased.

articles.headline: Court allows CBI further probe into NEET-UG paper leak case
articles.summary: A Delhi court allowed the CBI to conduct further investigation into the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case and add additional forensic evidence. The court noted that certain co-conspirators were yet to be identified and their roles established. The CBI has already filed a charge sheet against several individuals for their involvement in leaking the exam paper to candidates for large sums of money.

articles.headline: Odisha appoints acting DGP as selection process remains stalled
articles.summary: The Odisha government appointed a senior IPS officer as the acting Director General of Police (DGP) after the regular selection process was stalled by a court order. The appointment comes as the incumbent DGP retires on August 15. The state government had proposed a list of officers to the UPSC, but the process was deferred following a legal challenge regarding the selection criteria.

articles.headline: Delhi HC rules live Gurbani broadcast not copyright breach
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court ruled that the live broadcasting of Gurbani from the Golden Temple for religious purposes does not constitute a copyright infringement. The court dismissed a plea by a private channel seeking to restrain others from broadcasting the prayers. The bench stated that religious ceremonies are for the public good and cannot be restricted by commercial copyright claims.

articles.headline: Tension in Assam's Sribhumi over local BJP leader's murder
articles.summary: Tension flared in Assam's Sribhumi district after the body of a 52-year-old local BJP leader was found in a pond. Six people have been detained for their alleged involvement in the murder, which police believe was the result of a personal enmity. The victim had been missing for two days before his body was recovered. Security has been beefed up in the area to prevent any communal unrest.

articles.headline: US announces tariffs of up to 100% on Chinese drones
articles.summary: The US is imposing tariffs of up to 100% on Chinese-made drones, citing concerns over national security and the need to protect domestic industries. The move targets major Chinese drone manufacturers like DJI. US officials stated that the dependence on Chinese technology for critical infrastructure and surveillance poses a risk, and the tariffs would encourage local production and innovation.

articles.headline: Record rains in Japan kill 8 and strand thousands of travellers
articles.summary: Catastrophic rainfall in Japan has caused widespread flooding and landslides, leading to eight confirmed deaths. Thousands of travelers were stranded as major highways and rail lines were submerged or blocked. More than 20,000 homes were left without power, and emergency teams are working to rescue those trapped in their houses. Authorities have warned of more rain in the coming days.

articles.headline: US aircraft carrier sailors face mental strain from long deployment
articles.summary: Sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln are experiencing significant mental health issues and fatigue due to an extended deployment in the Middle East. The ship has been stationed in the region for several months beyond its original schedule. US Navy officials stated they are providing additional support and counseling to the crew, but the strain highlights the challenges of long-term maritime presence.

articles.headline: Toxic gas leak kills 8 workers in Bangladesh shipbreaking yard
articles.summary: A suspected toxic gas leak at a shipbreaking yard in Bangladesh resulted in the deaths of eight workers during the dismantling of a decommissioned vessel. Several other workers were injured and are receiving treatment in hospitals. Shipbreaking is one of the most dangerous jobs in the world, and this incident has once again highlighted the lack of safety standards in the industry in South Asia.

articles.headline: India less exposed to AI job risks compared to peers: Goldman
articles.summary: A report by Goldman Sachs states that India's workforce is less vulnerable to job losses caused by artificial intelligence (AI) compared to other major economies. The report attributes this to India's high concentration of service-sector jobs that require human interaction and the relatively low adoption of advanced AI technologies in its labor market. However, it warned of long-term shifts in job roles.

articles.headline: India seek cricket reset under Gambhir and Gill in Galle
articles.summary: The Indian cricket team, under new head coach Gautam Gambhir, is preparing for a challenging Test series against Sri Lanka in Galle. The series is seen as a reset for the team as they look to qualify for the World Test Championship final. Captain Rohit Sharma and young star Shubman Gill are expected to play key roles in tackling the spin-friendly conditions in Sri Lanka.

articles.headline: Shubman Gill targets WTC final with series wins
articles.summary: Indian opening batsman Shubman Gill stated that the team needs to win at least six or seven of their next nine Test matches to secure a spot in the World Test Championship final. Gill, who has been in good form, emphasized the importance of winning matches both at home and away. He added that the team is focused on building a consistent and winning culture under the new coaching staff.

articles.headline: Jeff Bezos consortium buys minority stake in Liverpool FC
articles.summary: Fenway Sports Group has agreed to sell a minority stake in Liverpool FC to a consortium led by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. The deal, valued at several hundred million dollars, is expected to provide the club with additional capital for infrastructure development and player transfers. Bezos is the latest high-profile American billionaire to invest in a major European football club.

articles.headline: FCNR(B) Swaps to Close a Month Earlier due to Gush
articles.summary: RBI has advanced the deadline for mobilizing foreign currency non-resident (bank) deposits to August 31 from September 30. The scheme received $52.3 billion in inflows through FCNR(B) deposits as of August 13, significantly higher than expected, helping to bolster India's foreign exchange reserves and manage currency volatility.

articles.headline: SDTT Tells Tata Sons About Lack of Quorum for AGM
articles.summary: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT), one of the primary trusts controlling majority-owner Tata Sons, has informed the company it lacks the necessary quorum to hold its Annual General Meeting scheduled for Tuesday. The Maharashtra Charity Commissioner has not lifted curbs on some trustees, creating uncertainty over the meeting's status.

articles.headline: NDB Plans $7.5 Billion Funding to Deepen Rupee Lending
articles.summary: The New Development Bank (NDB) plans to channel $7.5 billion into India over five years to support infrastructure and sustainable development. The plan includes a $2.5 billion-equivalent rupee bond scheme to deepen local currency lending and help borrowers manage exchange-rate risks as India integrates further into the global economy.

articles.headline: Govt Notifies 40-Question Census 2027; Caste Status to be Recorded
articles.summary: The Indian government has notified the 2027 Census, which will feature a 40-question schedule. For the first time, it will include an open column to record sub-castes for Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) respondents. The census will collect demographic, socio-economic, and ID details, including Aadhaar and passport numbers.

articles.headline: Chamoli Tunnel Tragedy: Seven Dead and 19 Rescued
articles.summary: Seven workers died and 19 were rescued after debris entered an under-construction tunnel in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district following a landslide. Three people remain missing as rescue operations continue. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami is personally supervising the efforts involving NDRF, CISF, and SDRF personnel.

articles.headline: 1,057 Personnel Awarded Gallantry and Service Medals
articles.summary: A total of 1,057 personnel from the Police, Fire, Home Guard, and Civil Defence services have been awarded Gallantry and Service Medals on the occasion of Independence Day 2026. This includes President's Medals for Distinguished Service and Medals for Meritorious Service for their conspicuous acts of courage and dedication.

articles.headline: Fifty Tribal Freedom Fighter Villages to Showcase Tales of Valour
articles.summary: The government has identified 50 villages across India to be developed on the tourism map to showcase the history and sacrifices of tribal freedom fighters. Each village will receive up to ₹20 lakh for museums, memorials, and improved infrastructure to preserve the heritage of local heroes like Birsa Munda and Tantia Bhil.

articles.headline: BJP Opposes Karnataka Gutkha Ban over Impact on Areca Growers
articles.summary: The BJP in Karnataka has opposed the state government’s one-year ban on gutkha, claiming it will hurt 1.5 crore families dependent on areca nut cultivation. The party argues the move will negatively affect the livelihoods of farmers across eight districts who provide the raw material for the product.

articles.headline: Iranian President to Visit India for BRICS Summit Amid Shipping Tensions
articles.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will visit New Delhi for the 18th BRICS summit in September. Discussions with Prime Minister Modi are expected to focus on the development of the Chabahar Port and securing safe passage for commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing regional tensions and energy supply disruptions.

articles.headline: Badal Attack Accused Blames Former Government for Punjab Drug Crisis
articles.summary: Police state that Jaspal Singh, the man accused of attacking SAD chief Sukhbir Badal, was motivated by personal anger over the drug menace in Punjab. Singh reportedly blamed the previous SAD government for failing to tackle the crisis, which he claims has destroyed thousands of lives in the state. No links to extremist groups have been found.

articles.headline: NCP Leader Zeeshan Siddique Receives Death Threat via Voice Note
articles.summary: NCP leader Zeeshan Siddique has filed a police complaint after receiving a death threat from an individual claiming to be associated with the Rohit Godara gang. The threat was delivered via a voice note on his mobile phone from a Portugal-based number. Police are investigating the origin and authenticity of the message.

articles.headline: Google Debuts New Gemini Flash AI Model Amid Development Delays
articles.summary: Google has released Gemini 1.5 Flash, an AI model designed for speed and efficiency in tasks like summarization and coding. This release comes as the company faces delays with its more powerful Gemini 4 flagship model. Flash is aimed at providing a faster, lower-cost alternative for developers while incorporating new safety features.

articles.headline: Government Plans Single-Window Clearance System for India's Space Sector
articles.summary: The Department of Telecommunications and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting are considering a single-window clearance system for the space sector. This initiative aims to reduce red tape and streamline approvals from various ministries for satellite-based services, improving the ease of doing business for private space companies.

articles.headline: India Seeks Data-Sharing Pact with US to Tighten CSAM Crackdown
articles.summary: India is negotiating a formal data-sharing arrangement with the US to improve the investigation of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on social media platforms. Currently, US laws restrict tech giants from sharing data directly with foreign agencies, and the proposed pact aims to create a legal framework for faster information exchange.

articles.headline: AI Startup DeepSeek Raises Flagship Model Prices Ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek has increased the pricing for its flagship V4 models by more than four times current levels. This move signals a shift toward profitability as the company prepares for an initial public offering. Despite the price hike, DeepSeek's rates remain competitive compared to major US-based rivals.

articles.headline: India’s Wholesale Inflation Eases to 9.8% in July on Lower Energy
articles.summary: India’s wholesale price index (WPI) inflation eased slightly to 9.8% in July 2026 from 9.9% in June. The decline was primarily driven by softening global fuel and energy prices, which offset rising costs in the primary articles and manufacturing segments. Retail inflation also saw a marginal dip to 4.3% earlier in the month.

articles.headline: US Names India Among Nations Enabling Chinese Trade Bypass
articles.summary: The US has identified India and 40 other countries as "shadow transshipment networks" that allegedly allow Chinese products to bypass American tariffs. The annual value of these transshipped goods is estimated between $40 billion and $303 billion. The US plans to implement AI-based monitoring and stricter enforcement to curb this practice.

articles.headline: Government Increases Sugar Stock Scrutiny as Prices Hit Record Highs
articles.summary: The Indian government has increased monitoring of sugar stocks at mills and conducted physical verification as retail prices reach record levels. The move aims to ensure adequate domestic availability and prevent hoarding by bulk consumers and traders, with current sugar stocks estimated to be lower than in previous years.

articles.headline: Two Vessels Attacked in Strait of Hormuz Amid Isolation Warnings
articles.summary: Two commercial vessels were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, leading to a near standstill in maritime traffic. The US has warned Iran of unprecedented "economic isolation" if shipping routes are not secured. Regional tensions have surged as the UAE blames Tehran for the incident, while the US considers a naval blockade to protect energy supplies.

articles.headline: US President Orders Navy to Build Ships in Overseas Shipyards
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has ordered the Navy to build ships in foreign yards to accelerate fleet expansion and counter global maritime threats. This significant policy shift is aimed at addressing backlogs in domestic shipyards and will involve building new vessels in allied nations like Japan and South Korea to bolster naval capacity.

articles.headline: US Imposes 100% Levies on Chinese Drones to Accelerate Decoupling
articles.summary: The US administration has announced 100% tariffs on Chinese-made drones and their components. This move is part of a broader strategy to reduce reliance on Chinese supply chains and protect national security. The tariffs will apply to all drones weighing over 25 kilograms, significantly impacting the consumer and commercial drone market.

articles.headline: Kohler to Invest $100 Million in India Over Ten Years
articles.summary: David Kohler, CEO of Kohler Co., announced a $100 million investment plan for India over the next decade. The company targets the growing demand for premium bathroom and kitchen products, moving away from minimalist designs toward "maximalist" styles favored by Indian consumers. India is now Kohler’s second-largest market.

articles.headline: Quick Commerce Firms Plan 30-Minute Delivery for Large Electronics
articles.summary: Quick commerce companies like Blinkit and Zepto are partnering with manufacturers to offer 30-minute delivery for large appliances such as refrigerators and televisions. This initiative aims to disrupt the traditional retail and e-commerce markets by leveraging local dark stores and specialized delivery personnel for high-value goods.

articles.headline: Thermo Fisher Scientific Steps Up Investments in India Lab Infrastructure
articles.summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific is increasing its investments in India, focusing on local manufacturing and R&D for medical devices and bioprocess technologies. The company aims to capitalize on India's growing pharmaceutical and biotech sectors and is setting up a new lab facility in Bengaluru to support domestic and regional demand.

articles.headline: Trump-Branded Resort in Maldives Delays Launch of Digital Token
articles.summary: Plans to launch a digital token for a Trump-branded luxury resort in the Maldives have been postponed indefinitely. The project developers cited unfavorable market conditions and regulatory challenges as reasons for the delay. The token was intended to provide financing for the resort's development and offer investors fractional ownership.

articles.headline: Freedom and Flexibility are Non-Negotiable for Gen Z Employees
articles.summary: A study of Gen Z professionals in India shows that freedom at work, flexible hours, and remote options are prioritized over traditional job security and perks. This shift is forcing companies to rethink their management styles and workplace cultures to attract and retain young talent who value independence and direct control over their tasks.

articles.headline: Universities Launch 'Influencer' Degrees Amid Growing Creator Economy
articles.summary: Several universities in the US and Europe have launched undergraduate degrees in content creation and social media influence. These programs aim to provide students with skills in digital marketing, video production, and personal branding. However, critics argue about the academic value and long-term viability of such degrees.

articles.headline: Indian Markets End Lower for Third Consecutive Week on Regional Tensions
articles.summary: The Nifty 50 and Sensex closed in the red for the third straight week as tensions in West Asia and rising crude oil prices weighed on investor sentiment. Market participants remain cautious amid global economic uncertainty and are awaiting clearer signals on domestic corporate earnings and government policy directions.

articles.headline: ICICI Bank Seeks $1.45 Billion Loan from Bank of America Consortium
articles.summary: ICICI Bank is in advanced talks to raise $1.45 billion through a syndicated loan from a consortium of international banks led by Bank of America. The funds will be used to support the bank's international lending operations and take advantage of the RBI's special window for foreign currency-non-resident (bank) deposits.

articles.headline: Svatantra Microfin Files Draft Papers for ₹3,000 Crore Initial Offering
articles.summary: Svatantra Microfin, a leading microfinance institution backed by Ananya Birla, has filed draft papers for a ₹3,000 crore IPO. The offering includes a fresh issue of shares worth ₹1,500 crore and an offer for sale by existing investors. The proceeds will be used to expand the company’s loan portfolio and strengthen its capital base.

articles.headline: India to Start Men’s Hockey World Cup Campaign Against Wales
articles.summary: The Indian men’s hockey team will begin its quest for a World Cup title after 51 years as they face Wales in their opening match on Independence Day. The tournament marks a crucial milestone for the team, which has shown strong form in recent international competitions and is aiming to reclaim its place among the world's elite.

articles.headline: Bangladesh Opener Tanzid Hasan Hits Century on Test Debut vs India
articles.summary: Bangladesh’s Tanzid Hasan became the first batsman from his country to score a century on Test debut against India. His innings of 101 helped Bangladesh reach 351-6 at stumps on the opening day of the first Test match. Tanzid's performance was praised for its balance of caution and aggression against a world-class Indian bowling attack.

articles.headline: La Liga Kicks Off New Season Without Top Headlining Stars
articles.summary: The 2026-27 La Liga season has begun in Spain, although major clubs like Barcelona and Real Madrid are missing several key players due to recent international commitments. Despite the absence of some top stars, the league's opening weekend features several high-stakes matches and is expected to draw large crowds across the country.

articles.headline: Government to Launch PM Vishwakarma Scheme Phase 2
articles.summary: The Centre plans to launch the second phase of the PM Vishwakarma scheme on September 17, coinciding with the Prime Minister's birthday. The new phase will focus on improving loan accessibility and market linkages for traditional artisans. In the first phase, over 6 lakh beneficiaries received collateral-free loans totaling Rs 5,259 crore at a concessional interest rate of 5%.

articles.headline: New MMDR Bill Sparks Constitutional Row Over Mineral Taxes
articles.summary: The Mineral Laws (Amendment) Bill 2026 has reignited a dispute over states' rights to tax mineral wealth. Section 9D of the bill prevents state governments from imposing taxes or cesses on mineral rights without Central approval. Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren has written to PM Modi raising legal concerns, following a recent Supreme Court ruling that previously upheld states' powers in this domain.

articles.headline: Docon Sells 9.9% Stake in Thyrocare for Rs 986 Crore
articles.summary: Docon Technologies, a promoter of Thyrocare Technologies, sold a 9.9% stake in the diagnostics chain via bulk deals on the BSE and NSE for Rs 985.86 crore. The shares were sold at prices between Rs 624 and Rs 631.71. Following the transaction, Docon's holding in Thyrocare dropped from 60.92% to 51.02%. The sale saw participation from various institutional and global investors.

articles.headline: US Court Upholds $562 Million Award Against Antrix
articles.summary: A US Court of Appeals has upheld a $562.5 million arbitration award in favor of Devas Multimedia against Antrix Corporation, the commercial arm of ISRO. The court ruled that US courts have jurisdiction over the matter despite Antrix being a state-owned entity. Devas lawyers state the total claim, including interest, has now exceeded $2 billion following the 2011 cancellation of a satellite deal.

articles.headline: Geopolitical Tension Slows Sales Cycle for Indicabu
articles.summary: Indicabu Space Jet reported that the ongoing West Asia crisis has extended its sales cycle from three to five months. Geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain disruptions have also pushed interior costs up to Rs 1,650 per square foot from Rs 1,600. Despite the delays and rising raw material costs, the company expects to maintain a 30% revenue growth trajectory for the full year.

articles.headline: Mahindra to Expand Heavy Truck Network in India
articles.summary: Mahindra Group plans to add 15 new dealerships for its heavy commercial vehicle (HCV) segment over the next 12 months, targeting the Eastern and Western Indian markets. The integration of its truck and bus division aims to increase Mahindra's HCV market share from the current 3.5% to 5%. The company is also creating common workshops for its various commercial vehicle brands to improve service.

articles.headline: Retailers Expect High Footfall During Independence Day Weekend
articles.summary: Indian malls and retailers are anticipating double-digit revenue growth over the Independence Day long weekend. Major chains like Lifestyle and Biba are offering discounts of 50-60% to clear end-of-season stock. Retailers attribute the strong demand to positive consumer sentiment and government income tax incentives, which have boosted discretionary spending power for shoppers.

articles.headline: Kiwi Launches UPI Credit Line to Expand Reach
articles.summary: Fintech firm Kiwi has introduced a 'Credit Line on UPI' feature in partnership with banks like Axis and YES Bank. The company aims to acquire 5 million users by March 2026. This facility allows users to access credit up to Rs 50,000 directly through the UPI interface. The move follows NPCI's 2023 guidelines allowing banks to offer pre-sanctioned credit lines on the popular payment platform.

articles.headline: SEBI Proposes Digital KYC for Foreign Investors and NRIs
articles.summary: SEBI has issued a consultation paper proposing digital KYC for NRIs, OCIs, and foreign nationals without requiring their physical presence in India. If documents are verified via official databases, investors would be exempt from self-declaring their current address. The proposal aims to ease onboarding for individuals from FATF-compliant nations and boost foreign participation in Indian markets.

articles.headline: SEBI Plans Overhaul of Market Dispute Settlement Framework
articles.summary: Market regulator SEBI has proposed significant changes to its settlement mechanisms to ensure consistency and reduce legal delays. Key proposals include a new formula for calculating settlement amounts, removing the double-counting of ill-gotten gains, and reducing the re-filing fee for rejected applications from 50% to 20%. The move follows several high-value settlements involving major exchanges.

articles.headline: Bharat Forge Sees Robust Demand in Defense and Industrial Sectors
articles.summary: Bharat Forge reported a 16% growth in its industrial business and a 10% rise in overseas auto revenue for the June quarter. The company expects a strong second half in FY27 driven by demand for Class-8 trucks in North America. It bagged new orders worth Rs 1,352 crore in Q1, including defense contracts worth Rs 681 crore for advanced artillery systems and battle tank components.

articles.headline: Skyways Air Services Sets IPO Price Band
articles.summary: Skyways Air Services has fixed a price band of Rs 131 to Rs 138 per share for its Rs 582.80 crore initial public offering. The logistics firm's IPO includes a fresh issue of Rs 399 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 184 crore. The proceeds will be utilized for debt repayment and general corporate purposes. The company reported a net profit of Rs 63.52 crore in the 2025-26 fiscal year.

articles.headline: Technocraft Ventures Debuts at 46% Premium on Exchanges
articles.summary: Technocraft Ventures shares listed at a strong premium on Friday, closing at Rs 311.15 on the BSE, up 46.77% from the issue price of Rs 212. This gave the company a free-float market capitalization of Rs 258.79 crore. Conversely, Leap India shares had a weak debut, closing at Rs 145.10, which was 8.74% lower than its issue price of Rs 159.

articles.headline: Shiprocket IPO Subscribed Nearly 100 Times on Final Day
articles.summary: The IPO of e-commerce logistics aggregator Shiprocket saw massive investor interest, receiving 99.38 times total subscriptions. Institutional buyers led the surge with 122.8 times bids, followed by retail investors at 46.42 times. The platform received bids for 9.38 billion shares against an offer size of 94.4 million. The company aims to use the capital to scale its AI-driven delivery network.

articles.headline: Seven States Set Target for 1,380 New GCCs
articles.summary: Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Kerala, Haryana, and Tamil Nadu have set a collective goal to establish 1,380 new Global Capability Centers (GCCs) by 2031. According to a CBRE report, this move is expected to create 1.2 million new job opportunities. The states are leveraging specialized policies to attract multinational firms to set up hubs for technology and operations.

articles.headline: Defense PSU Launches High-Resolution 'Gud' Binoculars
articles.summary: India Optel Limited, a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, has launched 'Gud', a military-grade high-resolution binocular for the general public. Developed by the Ordnance Factory Dehradun, the binoculars feature a 7.6-degree field of view. The product is part of the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' initiative, bringing advanced optical technology to the domestic consumer market.

articles.headline: Exports to FTA Partner Nations Witness Robust Growth
articles.summary: India's exports to countries with which it shares Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) grew significantly in the first quarter of the current fiscal year. Exports to Singapore and Sri Lanka more than doubled. India currently has 17 active FTAs, including deals with the UAE, Australia, ASEAN, and South Korea. Trade data suggests that 16 of these agreements are driving high-volume export growth.

articles.headline: PM Internship Scheme Aims to Bridge Industry Skill Gap
articles.summary: Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that the PM Internship Scheme (PMIS) is designed to align youth skills with industry requirements. She noted that while vacancies exist, firms often find candidates lacking practical workplace behavior and teamwork skills. The FY27 budget allocated Rs 4,800 crore for the scheme, which will place interns in top firms like Infosys and Mahindra.

articles.headline: Bank Deposit Growth Reaches Highest Level Since 2016
articles.summary: Indian bank deposits grew by 15.4% as of July 31, the fastest pace since December 2016. Total deposits reached Rs 269.41 lakh crore, with an addition of Rs 6.61 lakh crore in the last fortnight. The growth was supported by the RBI's FCNR (B) swap facility, which allowed banks to attract foreign currency deposits more effectively. Demand deposits accounted for Rs 2.40 lakh crore of the growth.

articles.headline: Long-Term Bond Yields Drop Due to Supply Constraints
articles.summary: Yields on 15-year government bonds fell by 51 basis points to 6.94% since March as demand outstripped limited supply. Institutional investors like life insurance companies and EPFO have increased investments in long-term securities. The shift follows the RBI's neutral policy stance and expectations of stable interest rates, making long-term government debt more attractive to fund managers.

articles.headline: MHA Releases List of 40 Questions for 2027 Census
articles.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs has released 40 questions for the 2027 Census, which will include caste data for the first time in independent India's history. It will be the nation's first digital census, with citizen options to enter data via a portal. New queries cover mobile numbers, voter ID, digital literacy, and educational levels, aiming for a comprehensive demographic profile.

articles.headline: Congress Slams Government Over Census Question Design
articles.summary: The Congress party has criticized the Centre for failing to consult political parties on the 2027 Census questions. General Secretary Jairam Ramesh expressed concern that the lack of a standardized caste list would allow respondents to provide inconsistent data, undermining the survey's accuracy. Congress had advocated for a pre-prepared list similar to those used in Bihar and Telangana.

articles.headline: NITI Aayog Proposes National Policy for Caregiving Sector
articles.summary: With India's elderly population expected to hit 34.7 crore by 2050, NITI Aayog has proposed a national caregiving policy. The plan aims to formalize the sector by training 1.5 lakh caregivers and setting service standards. Currently, the sector is largely informal and dependent on women. The policy would create a national registry and digital platform to connect professional help with families.

articles.headline: RBI Official Calls for Simple and Empathetic KYC
articles.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Swaminathan J. emphasized that while KYC is essential for financial security and anti-money laundering, it should not become a burden for customers. He urged bank staff to assist customers in providing the correct documents and advocated for digital self-declarations for minor updates. He stressed that a successful KYC system balances rigid rules with human sensitivity.

articles.headline: BJP and Akali Dal Alliance Ends in Punjab
articles.summary: The BJP has officially announced that it will contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections alone, ending its decades-long partnership with the Shiromani Akali Dal. Following the split over farm laws in 2020, the BJP aims to build its own base. Meanwhile, the AAP is actively courted Hindu voters, while some Lok Sabha results indicate a resurgence of radical separatist sentiments in specific seats.

articles.headline: Landslide at Chamoli Hydel Project Leaves 7 Dead
articles.summary: Seven workers died and three remain missing after water and debris flooded an under-construction tunnel at the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti project in Uttarakhand. A landslide on Thursday evening caused the sudden inundation while 22 employees were inside. NDRF and ITBP teams rescued 19 individuals, but several bodies were recovered from the sludge. Search operations for the missing are ongoing.

articles.headline: Jharkhand Faces Protests Over Jobs and Poverty Failures
articles.summary: Student protests in Jharkhand have reached their 21st day, centering on exam paper leaks and high youth unemployment. Despite its vast mineral resources, Jharkhand remains one of India's poorest states. Protesters are demanding transparency in government recruitment. Analysis shows that while the state prioritized education spending after its formation in 2001, recent years have seen stagnation.

articles.headline: Independence Day Long Weekend Sees 20% Surge in Travel
articles.summary: Travel bookings for the Independence Day weekend have risen by 20% compared to last year. Gen Z and young professionals are driving demand for quick getaways to places like Uttarakhand and Jaipur. Bus travel bookings from Delhi increased by 53%, while hotel bookings grew by 21%. Industry experts noted a trend of last-minute bookings as travelers take advantage of the long weekend for tourism.

articles.headline: Water surge kills seven workers in Uttarakhand hydro tunnel
articles.summary: Seven workers died and 12 were injured after a surge of water and debris entered a THDC India hydro tunnel in Chamoli. Rescuers estimate 900 metres of the 4.5-km tunnel are filled with sludge and water. Three workers remain trapped. The site is part of the Pipalkoti area construction. Conditions remain critical for two survivors as manual search operations continue.

articles.headline: Andaman administration invites proposals for Green AI Data Centre on Nicobar
articles.summary: The Andaman and Nicobar administration has floated an expression of interest for a private-sector-led "Green AI/Data Centre Vertical." Potential locations identified include Campbell Bay and Hutbay. The project aims for seawater-based cooling and renewable energy. Local tribal communities on Great Nicobar Island have expressed concerns over the lack of public information.

articles.headline: Red Fort secured with anti-drone systems for 80th Independence Day
articles.summary: Security agencies have deployed 3,000 personnel and a 450-camera surveillance grid at Red Fort ahead of Independence Day. Measures include upgraded anti-drone systems and 80x zoom cameras. Security remains high following hoax bomb threats reported at the Delhi High Court and IGI Airport. Road closures around the historic site will be in effect from 4 a.m. to 11 a.m. on Saturday.

articles.headline: MCD standardises salaries for 4,400 multi-tasking staff from September
articles.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has approved a proposal to standardise the salaries of approximately 4,400 multi-tasking staff in its Health Department. Monthly pay will increase by nearly ₹10,000, bringing it in line with the ₹27,000 paid in other zones. Mayor Pravesh Wahi announced that the revised equal pay structure would be implemented starting September.

articles.headline: Former TMC MLA mobbed outside police station in R.G. Kar case
articles.summary: Former TMC MLA Nirmal Ghosh was attacked with eggs and muck by protesters while being escorted to a Barrackpore court. Ghosh was arrested for his alleged involvement in the hurried cremation of a doctor raped and murdered at R.G. Kar Medical College in 2024. The court remanded him to eight-day police custody. The incident occurred amid heavy slogans and garlands of shoes from the mob.

articles.headline: U.P. Village Panchayat Officer candidates threaten protest over results
articles.summary: Aspirants for the Village Panchayat Officer positions in Uttar Pradesh have announced an indefinite protest starting August 17 if the final merit list is not released. Candidates claim the result has been pending for three months, adversely impacting their lives. The protest is supported by the Sanyukt Pratiyogi Chhatra Hunkar Manch and will take place outside the selection commission.

articles.headline: Haryana farmers block toll plazas over murder of dairy worker
articles.summary: Farmer unions and khap panchayats blocked 27 toll plazas across Haryana to demand the arrest of suspects in the murder of dairy operative Jeevan Kundu. Protesters at 17 locations completely halted traffic, while others allowed free passage for vehicles for three hours. The family has refused to perform last rites until all accused are arrested. A call to oppose the CM's event was also issued.

articles.headline: BJD seeks special Odisha Assembly session to oppose mines Bill
articles.summary: Former Odisha CM Naveen Patnaik has demanded a special Assembly session to voice dissent against the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. Patnaik claims the Bill usurps the state's fiscal autonomy by granting the Centre sole authority over rules and restricting state power to levy taxes on minerals, which he termed a threat to constitutional rights.

articles.headline: Omar Abdullah cautions Centre against Gen Z-like protests in J&K
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah warned of youth-led agitations if the Cabinet report on revised reservation policies is not finalized soon. Abdullah expressed frustration over delays from the Lieutenant-Governor’s office regarding the 60:40 ratio between reserved and open categories. He also criticized the Indus Waters Treaty as "discriminatory" toward the Union Territory.

articles.headline: High Court orders probe into police excesses against Odisha tribal villagers
articles.summary: The Orissa High Court directed the Rayagada administration to report on alleged police brutality against tribal villagers opposing a bauxite mining project at Sijimali Hill. Petitioners alleged police ransacked homes and arrested 21 villagers, including 10 women, in early-hour raids. The court noted the police used UAPA against residents and directed the state to maintain peace.

articles.headline: Nagaland church body opposes order to sing Vande Mataram
articles.summary: The Nagaland Baptist Church Council has expressed opposition to a Central directive compelling citizens to sing the revised Vande Mataram at Independence Day events. The NBCC stated that while it respects national symbols, patriotism should be voluntary rather than compelled. It argued that compelling expressions of faith or conscience violates the pluralistic nature of the nation.

articles.headline: Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan alleges Mines Bill favours private monopolies
articles.summary: Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan claimed the Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill, 2026, encroaches on state constitutional powers and aims to weaken the public sector. He argued the legislation allows private corporations to reap windfall profits from sand mining. Both the ruling LDF and opposition UDF expressed concerns that the Bill restricts the state's power to levy taxes and cess.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav mocks U.P. government's cow urine procurement pilot project
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav took jabs at the Uttar Pradesh government's initiative to collect cow urine from farmers at ₹10 per litre. The pilot project in Bulandshahr aims to link cow protection with organic farming and rural income. Yadav called it another step toward a "one trillion economy." The government plans to expand the project and raise prices to ₹20 per litre.

articles.headline: Two villagers killed in Manipur attack by alleged Kuki extremists
articles.summary: Alleged Kuki extremists attacked Langka Naga village in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district, killing two people and injuring two others. The Working Committee of Tangkhul Naga Long claimed gunmen from the KNF and KRA were responsible. The attack led to a total shutdown in Liangmai Naga-inhabited areas. Security forces recovered 2,000 rounds of ammunition in subsequent searches in Kakching district.

articles.headline: Kharge demands answers on reported Chinese expansion in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge questioned the government over reports that the Chinese PLA has expanded its presence in Taksing and Shera-5 in Arunachal Pradesh. Kharge alleged the Prime Minister's "clean chit" to China emboldened transgressions and noted that traditional grazing grounds are now inaccessible. He demanded the restoration of the pre-May 2020 status quo on the border.

articles.headline: Mahua Moitra claims forced eviction from Nadia Circuit House at night
articles.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra alleged she was directed to vacate the Nadia district Circuit House late at night for "annual maintenance." Moitra stated she was served dinner before receiving a call to leave, noting a crowd was shouting outside the gates. The Nadia administration claimed the suspension of reservations was temporary, but opposition leaders raised security concerns.

articles.headline: States provide solar sops to reduce losses from electricity subsidies
articles.summary: Several states, including U.P. and Bihar, are providing financial aid for rooftop solar installations to reduce the burden of recurring power subsidies. Under the Utility-Led Aggregation Model, states treat additional subsidies as capital expenditure. As of August 13, 52 lakh households have installed Surya Ghar systems, aiming for the national target of one crore households by March 2027.

articles.headline: UAE condemns Iranian attack on ADNOC vessels in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: The United Arab Emirates has blamed Iran for attacks on two vessels linked to the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC). The UAE Foreign Ministry denounced the "hostile Iranian attack" that occurred while the ships were transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The incident has heightened regional tensions and impacts critical global energy supply routes.

articles.headline: India looks to revive Test Championship campaign in Galle opener
articles.summary: The Indian cricket team, led by Shubman Gill, begins a crucial two-match Test series against Sri Lanka in Galle. Currently fifth in the WTC standings, India needs multiple wins to secure a spot in the final. The match marks India's 600th Test. Key players include Yashasvi Jaiswal and Ravindra Jadeja, while Sri Lanka relies on left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya.

articles.headline: Praggnanandhaa crushes Jorden van Foreest to move into second place
articles.summary: Indian Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa defeated Dutchman Jorden van Foreest in the fourth round of the Sinquefield Cup. The win moves him to 2.5 points, sharing second place with three other players. Wesley So remains in the lead with 3 points. In the women’s Cairns Cup, Divya Deshmukh and Koneru Humpy played out draws, while Tan Zhongyi maintained her lead.

articles.headline: Sebastian Coe defends Olympic prize money for track and field winners
articles.summary: World Athletics President Sebastian Coe reiterated the importance of prize money for athletes, defending the $50,000 award for Paris gold medalists. Coe argued that financial stability supports athlete welfare and allows for better career planning. The inaugural Ultimate Championships in Budapest will feature a $10 million prize pot, with every competitor receiving financial rewards.

articles.headline: Kashmir's cricket bat industry faces crisis over willow shortage and climate
articles.summary: The ₹700-crore bat-making industry in Kashmir is struggling with a severe shortage of English willow timber, with prices rising from ₹300 to ₹1,250 per foot. Factors including drying wetlands, climate change, and timber smuggling to Punjab and Meerut are threatening production. The government has launched a drive to plant 2.2 lakh willow trees to meet the annual demand of 50 lakh bats.

articles.headline: Zambia resumes presidential vote count after pause due to staff attacks
articles.summary: The Electoral Commission of Zambia resumed counting ballots on Friday after a temporary suspension caused by attacks on polling staff and the theft of marked ballot papers. Tensions remain high across the country following Thursday’s presidential and parliamentary elections. The pause occurred after the ECZ reported incidents that compromised the safety of officials at counting centers.

articles.headline: Citizens urge CJI to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam
articles.summary: Over 100 public figures, including Arundhati Roy and Amitav Ghosh, have written to the CJI urging intervention for the release of activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. The letter notes the duo has been incarcerated for nearly six years without trial under UAPA. It invokes the Supreme Court’s Najeeb judgment, stating that prolonged detention violates the fundamental right to a speedy trial.

articles.headline: India’s Q1 exports shift toward Asian and emerging markets
articles.summary: Merchandise exports showed growth in shipments to the ASEAN bloc and North-East Asia in Q1 FY27. Exports to Singapore more than doubled to $6.52 billion, while dispatches to China rose 27% to $5.59 billion. Trade experts cite a strategic shift as Indian firms find high growth in Asian regions compared to traditional markets like Europe and NAFTA.

articles.headline: RBI to end concessional FCNR(B) swap window on August 31
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India will close its concessional swap facility for Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposits a month earlier than planned. The window, which attracted $52.30 billion between June 8 and August 13, will revert to old interest rates of about 3% from September. The move is seen as a calibration as inflow targets have been achieved.

articles.headline: Indian student numbers in US hit 29-month low
articles.summary: The number of Indian students in the US fell to 3,38,230 in July, the lowest in 29 months, amid visa delays and immigration policy changes. US Homeland Security data shows a 10-month decline, with Master’s student numbers dropping 11.3% year-on-year. Experts suggest tighter immigration rules and a global tech slowdown have reduced the appeal of US education.

articles.headline: SEBI to overhaul settlement framework to reduce litigation
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) proposed a major overhaul of its 2018 settlement regulations to make proceedings faster and easier. Changes include a simpler formula for calculating settlement amounts, a fast-track mechanism for cases up to ₹10 lakh, and a 90-day window to apply for settlement. The move aims to cut settlement costs by 50%.

articles.headline: Noel Tata loyalists among top contenders to succeed N Chandrasekaran
articles.summary: Senior executives including Tata Steel's TV Narendran are emerging as candidates to lead Tata Sons after N Chandrasekaran's term ends. The search for a successor has begun, with Noel Tata's influence seen as significant. Loyalists from his inner circle, as well as family members like Neville Tata and Maya Tata, are being discussed for expanded roles within the group.

articles.headline: Voltas Q1 profit surges 51% on strong AC sales
articles.summary: Voltas Ltd reported a 51.3% increase in consolidated net profit to ₹212.76 crore for the June quarter, driven by robust performance in the cooling products segment. Revenue grew 18.65% to ₹4,673.5 crore. The company strengthened its leadership in the residential AC market with a 17.3% market share, benefiting from high summer demand.

articles.headline: Ashok Leyland announces ₹2,000 crore cost cutback drive
articles.summary: Facing commodity price pressures, Ashok Leyland has launched a ₹2,000 crore cost reduction program over the next 18-24 months. The company aims to maintain its ₹1,000 crore capex for FY27. Despite reporting its highest-ever Q1 net profit of ₹608 crore, EBTIDA margins dropped to 10% due to rising input costs. The firm plans to optimize product mix and efficiency.

articles.headline: New Range Rover and Defender to drive JLR's growth: CFO
articles.summary: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) expects the June quarter to be the low point for sales, with growth predicted to pick up in FY27. CFO Richard Molyneux stated that the upcoming four-product rollout, including the new Range Rover Electric, will drive the next level of growth. Despite a 9.6% drop in Q1 revenue to £5.97 billion, the company maintains its long-term investment plan.

articles.headline: Arvind Ltd taps Japanese designers to meet record denim demand
articles.summary: Textile major Arvind Ltd is collaborating with Japanese designers to capitalize on record-high denim demand. The company is operating at 100% capacity and is exploring an asset-light model to add capacity via leased units. Denim fabric volumes rose 34% year-on-year in the June quarter. The firm is also expanding its hubs in the US and UK to strengthen its international network.

articles.headline: July WPI inflation drops to 9.78% on easing food prices
articles.summary: Wholesale inflation in India dropped to 9.78% in July from 9.87% in June, the first month-on-month decline under the new 2022-23 base year. While food index inflation fell from 6.65% to 6.14%, manufactured products saw a slight uptick. Analysts expect WPI inflation to remain around 9.5-9.9% for the coming months as global commodity prices soften.

articles.headline: India's current account deficit widens to $6.2 billion in June
articles.summary: Preliminary data from the Reserve Bank of India shows the current account deficit widened to $6.2 billion in June, up from $1.2 billion a year ago. The widening was primarily due to a larger merchandise trade deficit, as imports rose to $71.4 billion while exports stood at $30.2 billion. Net services receipts rose to $17.9 billion, helping offset some trade losses.

articles.headline: Coal demand in India projected at 1.6 billion tonnes by 2030
articles.summary: India's coal demand is expected to reach 1.6 billion tonnes per annum by 2030, according to a top government official. To meet this, the government is setting up a Coal Exchange to allow transparent market-driven pricing. Coal production has already crossed 1 billion metric tonnes, with demand continuing to rise for power generation and industrial use.

articles.headline: Hormuz disruption raises shipping costs despite surging freight rates
articles.summary: Conflict in the Strait of Hormuz has added nearly $600 million in costs for shipping giants Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd in Q2 2026. Higher bunker fuel prices, insurance, and re-routing have led carriers to raise freight rates by up to 44%. Maersk's average freight rate increased 9% year-on-year, while shipping lines face higher operating expenses and vessel delays.

articles.headline: India remains world's fastest-growing major economy: President Murmu
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu, on the eve of the 80th Independence Day, highlighted India’s economic resilience. She noted that the country remains the world’s fastest-growing major economy, with a growth rate projected to be more than double the global average. She credited initiatives like 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' for strengthening the economy despite global geopolitical turmoil.

articles.headline: Amara Raja plans 10 GWh battery storage plant for revenue growth
articles.summary: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility expects its 10 GWh battery storage system (BESS) plant to generate $500-600 million in annual revenue within six months of commissioning. The company will invest ₹250-300 crore in the facility, focusing on iron phosphate cells. Management expects strong demand from grid-scale and commercial customers as India shifts toward renewable energy.
