articles.headline: SEBI eases InvIT cash flow distribution norms for infrastructure
articles.summary: SEBI has revised the framework for calculating net distributable cash flows (NDCF) for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs). The new rules allow trusts to add back certain debt-funded maintenance expenses to the cash available for distribution. This move, aimed at the roads and bridges sector, requires the project to have a maintenance agreement and specific unit-holder approval.

articles.headline: India heading for historic 50 GW solar installation this year
articles.summary: India is on track to add a record 50 gigawatts (GW) of solar power capacity in 2026, according to Wood Mackenzie. The surge is driven by the government's ALMM mandate and the phased removal of transmission charge waivers. In the first half of 2026, 34 GW was added, a 125% increase over 2025 levels. However, rising cell prices and supply chain constraints remain challenges.

articles.headline: Ministry lifts 12-minute TV ad duration cap for level playing
articles.summary: The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has removed the 12-minute-per-hour advertisement duration cap for television channels. The move aims to ensure a level playing field for broadcasters competing with digital media, which has no such restrictions. The ministry stated this would foster fair competition and allow the TV industry to better monetize its content.

articles.headline: SpaceX completes $60 billion acquisition of AI startup Cursor
articles.summary: SpaceX has finalized its $60 billion acquisition of AI startup Cursor, marking its largest foray into the AI sector. The deal, which closed on August 14, follows Elon Musk's goal of integrating advanced AI into SpaceX's navigation and autonomous systems. Cursor's technology will be used to enhance mission planning and flight safety for future Mars missions.

articles.headline: Airbus report finds flight-control malfunction in IndiGo flight incident
articles.summary: An initial Airbus report into a Phuket-Delhi IndiGo flight incident on August 4 identified a temporary malfunction in the aircraft's triple flight-control systems. The A320neo suffered a sudden loss of altitude during flight. Investigators are examining hydraulic systems and control transducers. The DGCA is expected to release a full safety report within 15 days.

articles.headline: Fractal Analytics launches India's first healthcare AI model, Vaidya.ai
articles.summary: Fractal Analytics has launched Vaidya.ai, a healthcare-focused AI reasoning model under the IndiaAI Mission. The model, being piloted with the Mumbai municipal corporation, provides AI-guided consultations for doctors and simplifies medical reports for patients. It is designed to work in local languages like Hindi and Marathi, outperforming OpenAI's models in healthcare tests.

articles.headline: US considers economic pressure on Iran following Hormuz ship attacks
articles.summary: The US may increase economic sanctions on Iran after fresh attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz caused a standstill in maritime transit. Nine ships passed through the narrow waterway on Thursday, down from the usual 130. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated the Navy has the capacity to maintain a presence to protect global energy supply chains from interference.

articles.headline: Indonesia to launch new commodity bourse for nickel and coal
articles.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto announced plans to create a new commodity exchange to set prices for the country's mineral exports like nickel, coal, and tin by 2027. The move aims to increase national revenue and move away from global benchmark prices. The exchange will also cover copper and palm oil, aiming to make Indonesia a "price-setter" for its resources.

articles.headline: China's Z.ai claims GLM-5.3 model excels in cyber-defence tests
articles.summary: Beijing-based Z.ai reported its new GLM-5.3 AI model outperformed Anthropic’s Mythos 5 in identifying software vulnerabilities. In tests, GLM-5.3 scored 84.5% in identifying and exploiting bugs, compared to 78% for Mythos 5. The model is aimed at strengthening national cybersecurity, though experts note such tools could also lower barriers for attackers.

articles.headline: Chinese astronauts successfully harvest first batch of space-grown rice
articles.summary: Astronuts on the Shenzhou-23 mission have harvested the first batch of rice grown on the Chinese Space Station. The experiment, using seeds taken to space in May, aims to study the genetic stability and productivity of rice in microgravity. This marks a breakthrough in long-duration space mission food support, with the harvested seeds to be brought back for further study.

articles.headline: Weather forecast warns of 90% risk of strong El Nino
articles.summary: Climate forecasters have warned of a 90% chance of a very strong El Nino event occurring during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter of 2026-27. The phenomenon, caused by warming ocean waters in the Pacific, could disrupt global weather patterns, potentially leading to droughts and floods. The impact on agriculture and energy prices remains a key concern for 2027.

articles.headline: Nissan Tekton review: A strong contender in the SUV market
articles.summary: The new Nissan Tekton SUV, priced between ₹10.49 lakh and ₹18.59 lakh, aims to challenge leaders in the C-segment. Built on the same platform as the Renault Duster, it features 1.0-litre and 1.3-litre turbo-petrol engines. The top-tier Tekna+ variant includes 17 ADAS functions, a 10.25-inch digital cockpit, and a panoramic sunroof, offering a premium interior and competitive safety.

articles.headline: Aprilia Tuono 457 review: A street-friendly evolution in performance
articles.summary: The Aprilia Tuono 457 is a street-focused evolution of the RS 457, featuring a 47-bhp parallel-twin engine. Changes include a redesigned seat, increased handlebar height, and recalibrated suspension for better comfort on city roads. Priced at ₹3.99 lakh, the motorcycle offers a more accessible and upright riding position while maintaining its heritage of sharp handling.

articles.headline: Centre orders sugar mills to report bulk sales data by August 20
articles.summary: The Union government has directed sugar mills to provide data on bulk sales within seven days of transactions to check price surges. Mills must identify buyers holding stocks beyond allocated quotas. The directive, effective until November 30, aims to prevent artificial scarcity and ensure that sugar prices, which have risen 8% in the retail market, remain stable.

articles.headline: Pulses acreage in India remains on par with last year
articles.summary: Total pulses acreage in India stands at 108.1 lakh hectares, nearly identical to last year's level. Higher sowing was recorded in Gujarat and Rajasthan, while Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh saw declines due to uneven rainfall. Pigeon pea (Tur) area rose 2% to 40.3 lakh hectares. Trade experts hope for good September rains to maintain crop yields and stabilize market prices.

articles.headline: NMDC reports 2% profit growth on strong iron-ore sales
articles.summary: State-owned NMDC Ltd posted a 2% rise in consolidated net profit to ₹2,005.71 crore for the June quarter. Total income rose to ₹7,142.54 crore, supported by higher revenue from iron ore sales. The company achieved a 10% growth in iron ore production and sales during the April-June period, despite fluctuations in global commodity prices and market demand.

articles.headline: Digital governance is transformative for citizens, says Amitabha Ranjan
articles.summary: Digital public infrastructure (DPI) in India has significantly reduced corruption and improved service delivery through initiatives like GeM and GSTN. The direct transfer of benefits (DBT) has eliminated middle-men, saving the government billions. However, experts warn that the use of AI and algorithms in governance must remain transparent to avoid becoming "black box" systems.

articles.headline: New FCRA rules bring stricter oversight for Indian NGOs
articles.summary: The 2026 overhaul of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) introduces a more central authority model for monitoring non-profits. The new rules mandate a one-year declaration period for foreign funding use and impose stricter registration renewals. While aimed at preventing misuse of funds, critics argue the concentrated power could impact grassroots social work organizations.

articles.headline: Health insurance reforms must address rising cost of medical care
articles.summary: Experts at the NHCX summit emphasized that health insurance reforms should move beyond premium rates to address the underlying cost of healthcare. Standardizing treatment protocols and common platform interfaces could reduce hospital and administrative costs by 5-10%. The focus should be on making quality care affordable for middle-income households through better transparency.

articles.headline: Onam retail demand subdued amid rain and liquidity constraints
articles.summary: Retailers in Kerala report a slower-than-expected start to the Onam festival season due to rain and local liquidity issues. While white goods and appliance sales are down 35%, the garment sector expects a 15-20% growth in the final 10 days of the season. Traders hope for a last-minute surge in consumer spending to reach last year’s festive revenue levels.

articles.headline: Maharashtra FDA cracks down on unlicensed quick-commerce food units
articles.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licenses of 14 food establishments linked to quick-commerce platforms like Blinkit and Zepto. An inspection drive found violations related to food safety, hygiene, and storage conditions. The regulator has directed platforms to strictly adhere to FSSAI standards for food safety and licensed operations.

articles.headline: Gold can become a key pillar of India’s growth story
articles.summary: The World Gold Council (WGC) suggests that gold could be a significant growth driver for India as the nation works toward 'Viksit Bharat 2047'. The report recommends creating a Gold Board of India to streamline the industry and boost jewelry exports. Domestic gold demand remained stable despite price increases, with the industry needing modernization to attract global consumers.

articles.headline: Technocraft IPO jumps 47%, Leap India tumbles on market debut
articles.summary: Shares of Technocraft Ventures saw a strong listing on the NSE, ending its first session 47% above its issue price at ₹311.15. In contrast, Leap India had a muted debut, closing 9% below its issue price at ₹143.90. The contrasting performances highlight selective investor interest in the mid-cap segment and varying demand for different business models.

articles.headline: Minda Corp's Q1 profit grows 33% on strong performance
articles.summary: Minda Corp reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of ₹1,850 crore for Q1 FY27, a 33% year-on-year increase. EBITDA rose 35% to ₹210 crore. Growth was driven by strong performance in the wiring harness and instrument clusters segments. The company continues to outperform the automotive industry, supported by a healthy order book and expanding product portfolio.

articles.headline: HAL shares gain on positive Q1 results and order outlook
articles.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) shares rose as the company reported a healthy 14.4% year-on-year growth in Q1 revenue. EBITDA margins expanded to 27.7%, supported by lower expenses. With an order book of approximately ₹90,000 crore and major projects like the LCA Mk1A and engine manufacturing programs on track, analysts maintain a 'BUY' rating on the stock.

articles.headline: Juniper Hotels to invest ₹850 crore in new luxury project
articles.summary: Juniper Hotels plans to invest ₹850 crore to develop a new 550-room luxury hotel in New Delhi, scheduled for completion by 2030. The project, located near the Yashobhoomi Convention Centre, will be a five-star facility. The company has executed a lease agreement with the DDA for the project, aiming to capitalize on the rising demand for premium business travel.

articles.headline: PNB signs deal with Geyftr to boost credit card engagement
articles.summary: Punjab National Bank (PNB) has entered a three-year agreement with the rewards platform Geyftr. Under the deal, Geyftr will build a white-label digital platform for PNB's credit card customers, offering curated deals and rewards. This partnership aims to increase credit card usage and customer engagement through a more personalized and diverse range of offers.

articles.headline: Just In Time eyes ₹1,000 crore revenue by FY27
articles.summary: Multi-brand watch retailer Just In Time is targeting ₹1,000 crore in annual revenue by FY27 as it expands its retail footprint. The company plans to add another 100 stores to its existing network of 100 outlets. CEO Raunak Shah noted that demand for premium and bridge-to-luxury watches remains strong, particularly in the ₹10,000 to ₹2 lakh price range.

articles.headline: Airtel Money considers UK listing in US dollars
articles.summary: Airtel Africa Plc is exploring a potential listing for its mobile money business, Airtel Money, on the London Stock Exchange in US dollars. The listing, which could happen as early as next year, aims to unlock the value of the unit, which is valued at up to $10 billion. The company is in talks with advisors to manage the initial public offering.

articles.headline: Demand destruction cushions impact of global oil price spikes
articles.summary: High global oil prices are leading to "demand destruction" as consumers in major markets like India and China reduce fuel consumption. This shift has helped cushion the impact of supply shocks caused by geopolitical tensions in West Asia. Experts suggest that higher prices are forcing a more rapid transition to electric vehicles and improved fuel efficiency in the long term.

articles.headline: AI emerges as revenue pool but not yet growth engine: Gartner
articles.summary: Indian IT services firms are increasingly generating revenue from AI and GenAI projects, but the segment is not yet a major growth driver. Analysis by Gartner shows that while AI-related services are growing, they represent a small percentage of total revenue for firms like TCS and Infosys. High investment costs and talent shortages continue to limit the overall impact of AI on growth.

articles.headline: SEA report: 70% of global ricebran oil potential remains untapped
articles.summary: A report by the Solvent Extractors’ Association of India (SEA) states that 70% of the world’s ricebran oil potential is currently untapped. While India is a leading producer, there is a potential to produce 2.3 million tonnes of ricebran oil compared to the current 1.1 million tonnes. Tapping this potential would require better rice-milling infrastructure and incentives for bran stabilization.

articles.headline: Kochi auctions see rise in orthodox tea demand from West Asia
articles.summary: Easing tensions in West Asia have led to a revival in demand for orthodox tea at Kochi auctions. Larger leaf-grade prices rose by ₹3-5 per kg, reflecting improved buyer sentiment from the CIS and West Asian markets. Despite a general slowdown in the sector, the positive outlook for exports has provided a boost to tea planters and exporters in South India.

articles.headline: ISMA and ICAR to set up ₹80-crore cane research centre
articles.summary: The Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) and ICAR-IISR are setting up a ₹80-crore research centre for high-quality sugarcane seed production. The centre aims to improve sugarcane yields and sugar recovery through better seed technology and pest-resistant varieties. This initiative will support sugar mills in improving their productivity and sustainability.

articles.headline: Mumbai to host CLFMA annual meet on September 11-12
articles.summary: The Compound Livestock Feed Manufacturers Association (CLFMA) will hold its 59th annual general meeting in Mumbai on September 11-12. The event will focus on 'Animal Agriculture - The Next Frontier of Development' and will bring together industry leaders, researchers, and policymakers. Discussions will center on food security, sustainability, and the role of the animal agriculture sector.

articles.headline: Drug kingpin Basoya extradited from UAE in Rs 13,000cr cocaine case
articles.summary: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has secured the extradition of Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE. Basoya is allegedly linked to India's largest-ever cocaine seizure worth Rs 13,000 crore. He was detained via an Interpol Red Corner Notice and was flown to Delhi to face charges involving a transnational drug trafficking syndicate and money laundering operations.

articles.headline: France's top court blocks bill banning social media for under-15s
articles.summary: France's constitutional court has blocked a legislative attempt to ban social media access for children under the age of 15. The court ruled that the proposed bill infringes on the fundamental freedom of expression and communication. President Emmanuel Macron's government has been asked to rewrite the legislation to address these constitutional concerns.

articles.headline: Chamoli landslide toll reaches seven as rescue operations continue
articles.summary: The death toll from a massive landslide at a hydroelectric project site in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district has risen to seven. Three workers remain missing under the debris. Rescue teams from the SDRF and local authorities are working to clear thick sludge and rock from an under-construction tunnel. Heavy rains have slowed the operation as officials fear more slides.

articles.headline: Noida boy allegedly kills father and jumps before Metro train
articles.summary: A 16-year-old boy allegedly killed his father at their home in Noida and subsequently committed suicide by jumping in front of a Metro train at the City Centre station. Police officials stated the boy was reportedly upset with his father over undisclosed domestic issues. Investigations are ongoing to determine the exact motive behind the murder-suicide incident.

articles.headline: HC says homeless child victims cannot provide precise crime details
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court upheld the conviction of a man for sodomizing an 11-year-old homeless boy, ruling that child victims living on the street cannot be expected to provide precise details like time or dates. The court noted that minor discrepancies in testimony are natural for a child who has undergone trauma and lacks the stability of a settled home environment.

articles.headline: MEA advises Rahul Gandhi to respect strong India-Italy relations
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs has urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to be mindful of the strong ties between India and Italy following his recent jibes at the Italian government. Officials emphasized that foreign policy should be based on mutual respect and that domestic political rhetoric should not damage long-standing international partnerships and diplomatic protocols.

articles.headline: Blood donation camps ruled taxable under GST by Gujarat AAR
articles.summary: The Gujarat Authority for Advance Ruling (AAR) has ruled that organizing blood donation camps does not qualify as a charitable activity exempt from GST. The ruling stated that although such camps save lives, the service of organizing them falls within the definition of taxable commercial activities. This decision may lead to increased costs for NGOs and hospitals hosting such events.

articles.headline: Defence ministry signs Rs 1,577 crore deal for loitering munitions
articles.summary: In a major boost to 'Atmanirbhar Bharat,' the Indian Defence Ministry has signed contracts worth Rs 1,577 crore with two Indian companies for loitering munitions. Also known as 'suicide drones,' these systems are designed to hover over a target and strike with precision. The deals were signed with Tata Advanced Systems Limited and Pune-based NIBE Private Limited.

articles.headline: India's youth population of 371 million to drive future growth
articles.summary: With 371 million people aged 15 to 29, India is now home to the world's largest youth population. Economists suggest this demographic dividend offers a unique opportunity for economic growth through innovation and digital transformation. However, experts warn that success depends on bridging the gap between education and employability to meet the demands of a modern global economy.

articles.headline: RBI to close $52.3bn FCNR(B) deposit scheme early after strong response
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to close its special FCNR(B) swap facility on August 31, a month earlier than planned, after banks raised over $52.3 billion in deposits. The scheme was launched to shore up foreign exchange reserves and provide dollar liquidity. Analysts suggest the overwhelming response reflects strong global investor confidence in India's macro stability.

articles.headline: Claude and Gemini AI apps see massive download surge in India
articles.summary: Generative AI applications Claude and Gemini recorded explosive growth in India during the second quarter. Claude's downloads jumped 30-fold, while Google's Gemini saw its user base double. The surge is attributed to the increasing use of AI for professional and creative tasks. Despite the high download volume, monetization remains a challenge as most users stick to free versions.

articles.headline: FMCG companies report recovery in rural and urban consumption
articles.summary: Major Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) companies, including Nestle and Marico, have reported a recovery in consumption growth for the April-June quarter. Volume growth has improved in both rural and urban markets as inflationary pressures ease. Companies expect this momentum to continue into the festive season, although rising raw material costs remain a key monitoring factor.

articles.headline: Zetwerk promoters to pledge 32% stake ahead of major IPO
articles.summary: The promoters of manufacturing unicorn Zetwerk plan to pledge 32.2% of their combined holding to secure funds for the company's upcoming Initial Public Offering (IPO). The IPO is expected to include a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,600 crore. The move is intended to provide the necessary capital for business expansion and to provide an exit for some early-stage investors.

articles.headline: Trump approves overseas ship building for US Navy carriers
articles.summary: In a major policy shift, President Donald Trump has signed a memorandum allowing the US Navy to build components for its next-generation aircraft carriers at shipyards abroad. The order also mandates the return to steam-powered catapult systems, replacing the problematic Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS). The decision is aimed at reducing costs and speeding up deployment.

articles.headline: 17-year-old PIO kills mother and brother in US family tragedy
articles.summary: A 17-year-old Indian-origin boy in Boston allegedly killed his mother and 14-year-old brother before attempting suicide. Investigators found evidence that the teen had been using generative AI tools to script 'theories' and 'fantasy stories' regarding the killings. The case has sparked a debate in the US about the potential psychological impact of AI on vulnerable minors.

articles.headline: US readies new economic isolation plan for Iran
articles.summary: The US government is preparing a new set of economic sanctions against Iran to further isolate its economy and curb its nuclear program. The plan includes measures to restrict Iran's oil exports and financial transactions with international partners. US officials stated that the 'one-two punch' strategy aims to increase pressure on Tehran to return to the negotiating table for a new nuclear deal.

articles.headline: NSE readies mega IPO, targets mid-September launch
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) is preparing for its much-awaited initial public offering (IPO) in mid-September. The exchange is aiming for a valuation of approximately $25 billion, which would make it one of India's largest-ever IPOs. The move follows regulatory clearances and a surge in retail investor participation in the Indian stock market. The IPO is expected to be a major boost for the financial sector.

articles.headline: CJI and students question Bar Council over protest circular
articles.summary: The Supreme Court, led by CJI Surya Kant, has questioned the Bar Council of India (BCI) for a circular that threatened to debar Nalsar University students from practicing law if they protested against the CJI's visit. The CJI stated students have a right to peaceful protest. BCI has since withdrawn the letter following massive backlash from alumni and the legal fraternity.

articles.headline: Reliance and Rolls-Royce eye developing engine for stealth fighter
articles.summary: Reliance Industries and Rolls-Royce have announced plans to jointly develop a powerful engine for India's fifth-generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA). The partnership aims to build an indigenous engine ecosystem in India, which would enhance the country's self-reliance in critical defense technologies. The project is expected to involve significant investment and technology transfer.

articles.headline: 7 dead, 3 trapped in latest Himalayan hydropower project mishap
articles.summary: Seven workers died and three remain trapped after a suspected aquifer burst sent water and debris through a hydropower tunnel in Chamoli, Uttarakhand. Rescue teams from the NDRF, SDRF, and Army are searching for the missing men in the flooded Vishnugad-Pipalkoti project tunnel. Of the 22 workers on shift, 12 were admitted with injuries while seven deaths were confirmed.

articles.headline: Zee Entertainment Gets SAT Nod to Raise Rs 3,143 Crore
articles.summary: The Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) has granted interim relief to Zee Entertainment (ZEEL), allowing it to raise Rs 3,143 crore through preferential warrants. While the SAT upheld SEBI's ban on Punit Goenka from the securities market for 12 months, it permitted the use of mutual fund units for business needs. SEBI had previously blocked the fundraise citing alleged diversion of company funds.

articles.headline: India Balance of Payments Hits $8.1 Billion Deficit
articles.summary: India's balance of payments (BOP) recorded a deficit of $8.1 billion in the April-June quarter of FY27, shifting from a $4.5 billion surplus a year earlier. The RBI attributed the deficit to a current account gap of $3.1 billion and a net outflow of $5 billion from the capital account. Portfolio investment shifts were a major factor in the quarterly deficit compared to the previous year.

articles.headline: Zetwerk plans to raise rs 2,600 crore in updated IPO
articles.summary: Tech-led manufacturing platform Zetwerk has updated its IPO plans to raise Rs 2,600 crore through a fresh issue of shares. The company intends to use the proceeds for business expansion and to invest in its global manufacturing network. Zetwerk has seen significant growth in recent years as more companies look to diversify their supply chains outside of China.

articles.headline: CJI questions BCI's authority to stop NALSAR student enrolments
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant questioned why the Bar Council of India (BCI) interfered in his dialogue with NALSAR students after they protested his convocation invite. The BCI had briefly ordered state councils not to enrol NALSAR's 2026 batch. The Supreme Court barred coercive actions against students, noting that the right to a profession cannot be threatened for expressing dissent.

articles.headline: SC dismisses FIRs against Suresh Raina and Samay Raina
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has dismissed FIRs filed against former cricketer Suresh Raina, comedian Samay Raina, and others for alleged remarks about persons with disabilities. The court noted that the individuals had already tendered apologies and showed a genuine effort to make amends. The bench described the group as 'bright youngsters' and urged them to be more careful in the future.

articles.headline: Two killed in firing at Naga village in Manipur
articles.summary: At least two individuals were killed after armed men opened fire at a village gathering in Manipur's Kangpokpi district. The victims were part of a Naga village community. Local reports suggest the attack was carried out by the Kuki National Front, leading to heightened tensions in the conflict-ridden region as security forces were deployed to maintain order.

articles.headline: Census set to seek for first time caste, Aadhaar, other IDs
articles.summary: The Union government notified 40 questions for the upcoming census, including requests for Aadhaar numbers, mobile numbers, and voter IDs for the first time. The exercise will also record the caste of individuals as declared, without a pre-prepared list, marking a significant change in data collection. Self-enumeration begins on August 17 in certain high-altitude regions.

articles.headline: Supreme Court stays order quashing jobs for Karur stampede victims
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stayed a Madras High Court order that had struck down the Tamil Nadu government’s grant of jobs to family members of Karur stampede victims. Justice J.B. Pardiwala questioned why the state should not provide succour to families who lost breadwinners. A total of 41 people died in the September 2025 stampede during a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam roadshow.

articles.headline: Supreme Court quashes hate speech case against Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: The Supreme Court quashed a hate speech case against Rahul Gandhi regarding his 2022 remarks about V.D. Savarkar. The court ruled that the Uttar Pradesh government failed to grant the necessary sanction for prosecution under Section 196 of the CrPC. While quashing the Lucknow Magistrate's summons, the court cautioned Gandhi to avoid derogatory statements against freedom fighters.

articles.headline: RBI to close special foreign exchange swap window early
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced it will close a special foreign exchange swap window for banks on August 31, ahead of its scheduled September 30 expiry. The decision follows strong foreign currency inflows into FCNR(B) deposits, which have exceeded $52.3 billion. The early closure is part of the central bank's effort to manage domestic liquidity and foreign exchange reserves.

articles.headline: Pew Survey Shows Mixed Global Image for India
articles.summary: A Pew Research Center survey across 36 countries revealed that 42% of people have a positive view of India, while 36% hold negative perceptions. While India's image improved in Germany and Israel, it declined in the US from 51% to 45% between 2023 and 2026. In neighboring Bangladesh, 51% of respondents hold a positive view. The survey highlights shifting global opinions on India's leadership.

articles.headline: US Report Identifies India as Chinese Goods Transshipment Hub
articles.summary: A White House report has included India among 40 nations monitored for 'transshipment' risks, where Chinese goods allegedly bypass US tariffs. The report suggests products like pumps and compressors are routed through India to the US. It estimates that such schemes cost the US $28 billion in revenue. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs is currently reviewing the report's findings.

articles.headline: Nearly 30% of Delhi voters risk being struck off poll roll
articles.summary: Election officials in Delhi warned that approximately 30% of the city's registered voters may not be included in the draft poll roll due to verification issues. Verification of nearly 32% of voters is yet to be completed as the special intensive revision deadline approaches. Most unverified cases involve voters who are absent, shifted, or are dead, according to the poll body.

articles.headline: Karnataka plans bill to regulate use of public property for protests
articles.summary: The Karnataka government plans to introduce the 'Karnataka Regulation of Use of Government Premises and Public Property Bill, 2026' in the state assembly. The bill seeks to regulate the use of public spaces for protests, rallies, and religious gatherings, requiring prior permission and setting strict conditions. Violation of the rules could lead to imprisonment and fines.

articles.headline: President approves 78 gallantry awards including nine Kirti Chakras
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu approved 78 gallantry awards for personnel of the armed forces and central armed police forces. The list includes nine Kirti Chakras, of which seven were awarded posthumously, and 19 Shaurya Chakras. The awards recognize extraordinary bravery in anti-terror operations and peacekeeping missions across the country. 11 President’s Medal for Meritorious Service were also approved.

articles.headline: BJP MP Anant Maharaj booked for derogatory remarks on Netaji
articles.summary: Police in Kolkata registered an FIR against BJP Rajya Sabha member Anant Maharaj for making alleged derogatory remarks against Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. The complaint states that Maharaj referred to Netaji as a 'war criminal' in a video uploaded to social media. The BJP has distanced itself from the remarks, stating they are Maharaj's personal views and not the party's stand.

articles.headline: Nigel Farage regains UK seat amid challenge from Count Binface
articles.summary: Nigel Farage, the leader of the Reform UK party, regained his seat in the UK Parliament in a high-profile election. Interestingly, a satirical candidate named Count Binface secured nearly a quarter of the votes in the same constituency, highlighting public disillusionment with traditional politics. Farage stated his win is a mandate for his views on immigration and national sovereignty.

articles.headline: Italian police recover stolen Renoir, Cezanne and Matisse paintings
articles.summary: Authorities in Italy recovered three stolen masterpieces by Renoir, Cezanne, and Matisse, valued at millions of dollars. The paintings were stolen from a private museum in Parma and were recovered after a complex investigation involving international art experts. Three individuals have been arrested in connection with the theft, which was part of a larger ring targeting high-profile art collections.

articles.headline: Wholesale inflation in India cools to 9.78% in July
articles.summary: India's wholesale price index (WPI)-based inflation eased to 9.78% in July from 10.12% in June. The decline was primarily driven by lower prices for fuel and power, although food inflation remained high. Economists noted that while the cooling of wholesale prices is a positive sign, the Reserve Bank of India is likely to maintain a cautious stance on interest rates until retail inflation also stabilizes.

articles.headline: Ashok Leyland Q1 net profit rises 1.5% to rs 657 crore
articles.summary: Commercial vehicle manufacturer Ashok Leyland reported a 1.5% increase in its consolidated net profit to Rs 657.72 crore for the first quarter. The company's revenue from operations also saw a slight growth compared to the same period last year. Management stated that the results were driven by steady demand for heavy and medium commercial vehicles and improved operational efficiencies.

articles.headline: Jemimah Rodrigues ruled out of Asia Cup due to hand injury
articles.summary: Indian woman cricketer Jemimah Rodrigues has been ruled out of the upcoming Asia Cup and Asian Games after sustaining a hand injury during a training session. A medical assessment confirmed a minor fracture, requiring at least four weeks of rest. The BCCI is expected to announce a replacement shortly. Her absence is a blow to the team as she has been a consistent performer in the middle order.

articles.headline: Indian hockey team aims to end 51-year medal wait at World Cup
articles.summary: The Indian men's hockey team is determined to win a medal at the upcoming World Cup, a feat they have not achieved in 51 years. Led by Harmanpreet Singh, the team has been training intensively and has shown strong form in recent international matches. The players expressed confidence that their current tactical approach and physical fitness would help them compete with the world's best teams.

articles.headline: Churchill Brothers acquire Jamshedpur FC in major ISL deal
articles.summary: In a significant development for Indian football, Churchill Brothers have completed the acquisition of Jamshedpur FC. The move will see the historic Goan club participate in the Indian Super League (ISL). The deal includes the transfer of player contracts and infrastructure. Churchill Brothers stated that their aim is to build a competitive team that can challenge for the ISL title in the coming season.

articles.headline: Air India Flight Suffers Dual Hydraulic System Failure
articles.summary: An Air India Airbus A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi experienced a critical failure of multiple hydraulic systems on August 4. The aircraft was reportedly out of pilot control for four seconds, resulting in a sudden 300-foot altitude drop. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau is probing the incident, which involved 145 passengers. The plane landed safely in Delhi after systems stabilized.

articles.headline: President Murmu promises transparent and secure public examinations
articles.summary: On the eve of India's 80th Independence Day, President Droupadi Murmu addressed the nation, highlighting the youth as India's greatest asset. She stated that the government is undertaking comprehensive reforms to make public examinations transparent, secure, and free from paper leaks. She urged society to support the mental and physical well-being of the younger generation.

articles.headline: PhysicsWallah Narrows Net Loss to Rs 88 Crore
articles.summary: Edtech major PhysicsWallah reported a reduced net loss of Rs 88.28 crore for the first quarter of FY27. The company's total expenditure rose by 18.29% to Rs 1,247.02 crore as it expanded its operations. Despite the losses, the firm continues to see strong demand for its educational technology services, narrowing its deficit from over Rs 127 crore in the previous sequential quarter.

articles.headline: MakeMyTrip Partners with Tourism Ministry for Guided Tours
articles.summary: Travel platform MakeMyTrip has partnered with the Ministry of Tourism to offer guided tours across 60+ Indian cities. The collaboration will feature over 350 tours led by trained local guides and community experts. Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat stated the initiative aims to share India's cultural stories directly with travelers and strengthen the tourism service chain.

articles.headline: India’s forex reserves jump to record $707 billion
articles.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves increased by $14.136 billion to reach a new all-time high of $707.002 billion for the week ended August 7. The Reserve Bank of India data shows the overall kitty jumped from $692.866 billion the previous week. Foreign currency assets, a major component, rose by $9.946 billion to $574.625 billion during the same period.

articles.headline: India prepares for historic 600th Test match against Sri Lanka
articles.summary: The Indian cricket team is set to play its landmark 600th Test match when they face Sri Lanka in Galle. Under captain Shubman Gill, the team is focusing on a 'red-ball reset' after recent inconsistencies. The milestone match is expected to be a high-stakes encounter as India aims to improve its standing in the World Test Championship cycle and blood new talent.

articles.headline: Banwari Lal Engineering IPO Subscribed 108 Times
articles.summary: The initial public offering of Banwari Lal Engineering Limited closed with 108.44 times subscription. The QIB portion was subscribed 165.33 times, while the non-institutional segment saw 165.31 times demand. Retail individual investors bid 53.27 times for the available shares. The strong response reflects high investor interest in the industrial engineering and construction services sector.

articles.headline: President Murmu Addresses Nation on Independence Day Eve
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu addressed the nation on the eve of India's 80th Independence Day, promising major reforms to curb paper leaks in public examinations. She described students as the 'builders of the future' and highlighted India's rapid economic growth despite global conflicts. Murmu also celebrated the 150th year of 'Vande Mataram', urging a unified push toward a developed India by 2047.

articles.headline: India helping China evade U.S. tariffs, claims White House report
articles.summary: A White House report titled 'The Great Transshipment Scam' identifies India as one of 40 countries enabling Chinese exporters to route goods to evade U.S. tariffs. It specifically names the Pune-Gujarat-Chennai production belt as a hub for Chinese pumps and compressors. The U.S. may impose tariffs up to 100% on India for non-compliance regarding trade and forced-labour practices.

articles.headline: Delhi school cancels JNU professor's talk after protests over pluralism
articles.summary: Sardar Patel Vidyalaya in New Delhi cancelled a scheduled Independence Day talk by JNU Professor Emerita Zoya Hasan on 'Why pluralism matters.' The move followed protests from parents and groups identified as members of Vishwa Hindu Parishad. While the school cited 'unavoidable circumstances,' activists alleged the cancellation resulted from pressure over Hasan's ideological views.

articles.headline: MPD 2047 pushes for vertical growth and higher FAR in Delhi
articles.summary: The draft Master Plan for Delhi (MPD) 2047 has proposed significant changes to allow for vertical growth in the city. The plan includes increasing the Floor Area Ratio (FAR) and permissible building heights to accommodate a growing population and modern infrastructure. This shift aims to optimize land use and facilitate large-scale urban regeneration in both planned and unplanned areas.

articles.headline: Class 8 girl killed after DTC bus hits scooter in Delhi
articles.summary: A 12-year-old girl died in New Delhi's New Ashok Nagar after a DTC electric bus hit the scooter she was riding to school. The girl was riding pillion with her uncle when the bus struck them from behind. The driver has been arrested by the police. Following the incident, angry locals and commuters vandalized the bus, leading to brief traffic disruptions in the area.
